facts.statement: The genus Kritosaurus was described by Barnum Brown in 1910.
facts.quote: authority: Brown, 1910

facts.statement: Kritosaurus lived approximately 74.5 to 66 million years ago during the Late Cretaceous period in North America.
facts.quote: It lived about 74.5-66 million years ago, in the Late Cretaceous of North America.

facts.statement: By 1916, Barnum Brown established that the fossils belonged to the late Campanian-age De-na-zin Member of the Kirtland Formation.
facts.quote: by 1916 was able to establish it as from what is now known as the late Campanian-age De-na-zin Member of the Kirtland Formation.

facts.statement: The 1914 description of the genus Gryposaurus led Barnum Brown to revise his reconstruction of Kritosaurus to include an arched nasal crest.
facts.quote: The 1914 publication of the arch-snouted Canadian genus Gryposaurus changed Brown's mind about the anatomy of his dinosaur's snout.

facts.statement: Barnum Brown synonymized the genus Gryposaurus with Kritosaurus, a classification supported by Charles Gilmore.
facts.quote: He also synonymized Gryposaurus with Kritosaurus, a move supported by Charles Gilmore.

facts.statement: Lull and Wright assigned the species Hadrosaurus breviceps to Kritosaurus, but this classification is no longer accepted.
facts.quote: The poorly known species Hadrosaurus breviceps (Marsh, 1889), known from a dentary from the Campanian-age Judith River Formation of Montana, was also assigned to Kritosaurus by Lull and Wright, but this is no longer accepted.

facts.statement: In 1984, José Bonaparte and colleagues named Kritosaurus australis based on fossils from the Los Alamitos Formation in Patagonia, Argentina.
facts.quote: In 1984, Argentine paleontologist José Bonaparte and colleagues named Kritosaurus australis for hadrosaur bones from the late Campanian-early Maastrichtian Los Alamitos Formation of Rio Negro, Patagonia, Argentina.

facts.statement: Analysis in 2022 proved that Kritosaurus australis belongs to a new genus named Huallasaurus.
facts.quote: In 2010, this species was thought to be a synonym of Secernosaurus koerneri. Further analysis proved the bones to belong to a new genus. Thus, Huallasaurus was named by Rozadilla et al. (2022).

facts.statement: In 1990, Jack Horner and David B. Weishampel separated Gryposaurus from Kritosaurus due to uncertainties regarding Gryposaurus's skull.
facts.quote: In 1990, Jack Horner and David B. Weishampel once again separated Gryposaurus, citing the uncertainty associated with the latter's partial skull.

facts.statement: Adrian Hunt and Spencer G. Lucas created the genera Anasazisaurus and Naashoibitosaurus for skulls that Jack Horner had claimed belonged to Kritosaurus.
facts.quote: Horner in 1992 described two more skulls from New Mexico that he claimed belonged to Kritosaurus and showed that it was quite different from Gryposaurus, but the following year Adrian Hunt and Spencer G. Lucas put each skull in its own genus, creating Anasazisaurus and Naashoibitosaurus.

facts.statement: Adrian Hunt and Spencer G. Lucas named the species Anasazisaurus horneri in 1993.
facts.quote: Adrian Hunt and Spencer G. Lucas, American paleontologists, named Anasazisaurus horneri in 1993.

facts.statement: The name Anasazisaurus is derived from the Anasazi people and the Greek word for lizard.
facts.quote: The name was derived from the Anasazi, an ancient Native American people, and the Greek word sauros ("lizard").

facts.statement: The holotype skull of Anasazisaurus horneri was collected in the late 1970s in San Juan County and is housed at Brigham Young University.
facts.quote: The holotype skull (and only known specimen) was collected in the late 1970s by a Brigham Young University field party working in San Juan County, and is housed at BYU as BYU 12950.

facts.statement: In 2002, a partial left maxilla from Big Bend National Park was assigned to Kritosaurus navajovius.
facts.quote: In 2002, specimen TxVP 41917–1, a partial left maxilla recovered from Bruja Canyon in Big Bend National Park, was assigned to Kritosaurus, as cf. K. navajovius.

facts.statement: In 2023, the specimen previously assigned to Kritosaurus was described as a new taxon named Malefica.
facts.quote: Twenty years later, it was discovered to contain a number of useful diagnostic traits that allow it to be described as a new taxon, and thus Malefica was named by Prieto-Márquez and Wagner (2023).

facts.statement: It is debated whether Kritosaurus is a valid genus, as some researchers judged it a nomen dubium due to a lack of diagnostic features.
facts.quote: Horner originally assigned the Anasazisaurus skull to Kritosaurus navajovius, but Hunt and Lucas could not find any diagnostic features in the limited material of Kritosaurus and judged the genus to be a nomen dubium.

facts.statement: Albert Prieto-Márquez regarded Anasazisaurus as a synonym of Kritosaurus but retained it as the species K. horneri.
facts.quote: Prieto-Márquez therefore regarded Anasazisaurus as a synonym of Kritosaurus, but retained it as the distinct species K. horneri.

facts.statement: A partial skeleton from the Sabinas Basin in Mexico was described as Kritosaurus sp. but later considered an indeterminate saurolophine.
facts.quote: A partial skeleton from the Sabinas Basin in Mexico was described as Kritosaurus sp. by Jim Kirkland and colleagues, but considered an indeterminate saurolophine by Prieto-Márquez (2013).

facts.statement: A partial skeleton from the Sabinas Basin is around 11 meters long, about 20% larger than other known specimens, and represents one of the largest well-documented North American saurolophines.
facts.quote: This skeleton is about 20% larger than other known specimens, around 11 meters [36 ft] long, and with a distinctively curved ischium, and represents one of the largest known well-documented North American saurolophines.

facts.statement: Kritosaurus fossils have been found in the Olmos Formation in Mexico.
facts.quote: Kritosaurus fossils have also been unearthed in the Olmos Formation in Mexico.

facts.statement: The type specimen of Kritosaurus navajovius consists of a partial skull, lower jaws, and associated postcranial remains.
facts.quote: The type specimen of Kritosaurus navajovius is only represented by a partial skull and lower jaws, and associated postcranial remains.

facts.statement: The remains indicate that Kritosaurus reached a body length of 9 meters and a mass of 4 metric tons.
facts.quote: However, these remains alone indicate a large body size, reaching 9 m in length and 4 MT in body mass.

facts.statement: A unique crest of bone rising between and above the eyes distinguishes Kritosaurus from similar hadrosaurs like Gryposaurus.
facts.quote: This unique crest allows it to be distinguished from similar hadrosaurs, like Gryposaurus.

facts.statement: Diagnostic features include a predentary without tooth-like crenulations, a sharp downward bend in the lower jaws, and a heavy, rectangular maxilla.
facts.quote: Potential diagnostic characteristics of Kritosaurus include a predentary (lower beak) without tooth-like crenulations, a sharp downward bend to the lower jaws near the beak, and a heavy, somewhat rectangular maxilla (upper tooth-bearing bone).

facts.statement: Kritosaurus was classified as a hadrosaurine hadrosaurid, characterized as a flat-headed or solid-crested duckbill.
facts.quote: Kritosaurus was a hadrosaurine hadrosaurid, a flat-headed or solid-crested duckbill.

facts.statement: Kritosaurus navajovius is the closest relative to Anasazisaurus horneri, and both belong to the clade Kritosaurini within Saurolophinae.
facts.quote: The closest relative of Kritosaurus navajovius is Anasazisaurus horneri (or Kritosaurus horneri), which, together with close relatives such as Gryposaurus and Secernosaurus, form a clade called the Kritosaurini within the larger clade Saurolophinae.

facts.statement: The habitat of Kritosaurus was interpreted as river floodplains that formed after the retreat of the Western Interior Seaway.
facts.quote: The Kirtland Formation is interpreted as river floodplains appearing after a retreat of the Western Interior Seaway.

facts.statement: Conifers were the dominant plants in the Kritosaurus environment, where chasmosaurine horned dinosaurs were more common than hadrosaurids.
facts.quote: Conifers were the dominant plants, and chasmosaurine horned dinosaurs appear to have been more common than hadrosaurids.

facts.statement: There is a debate regarding the age of the Kritosaurus holotype because the Ojo Alamo Formation is divided by an unconformity into older Campanian and younger Maastrichtian members.
facts.quote: However, not all of the paleontological community agrees with the age of the Kritosaurus holotype unearthed by Barnum Brown. This is due to the unconformity that divides the Ojo Alamo Formation into two parts; the older Naashoibito member, which overlies the Campanian era Kirtland Formation, and the younger Kimbeto member.

facts.statement: Kritosaurus was a large bipedal or quadrupedal herbivore that used a sophisticated skull for a grinding motion analogous to chewing.
facts.quote: As a hadrosaurid, Kritosaurus would have been a large bipedal/quadrupedal herbivore, eating plants with a sophisticated skull that permitted a grinding motion analogous to chewing.

facts.statement: Kritosaurus possessed dental batteries containing hundreds of teeth, with only a handful in use at any given time.
facts.quote: Its teeth were continually replacing and packed into dental batteries that contained hundreds of teeth, only a relative handful of which were in use at any time.

facts.statement: Kritosaurus fed on vegetation ranging from the ground up to approximately 4 meters (13 feet) high.
facts.quote: Feeding would have been from the ground up to ~4 meters (13 ft) above.

facts.statement: The top of the Kritosaurus crest is roughened, and the maximum preserved skull length could reach 90 centimeters.
facts.quote: The top of the crest is roughened, and the maximum preserved length of the skull could reach 90 cm.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest the nasal crest of Kritosaurus may have been used for social functions like identifying sexes, species, and social ranking.
facts.quote: The nasal crest of Kritosaurus, whatever its true form, may have been used for a variety of social functions, such as identification of sexes or species and social ranking.

facts.statement: It is hypothesized that inflatable air sacs flanked the crest for visual and auditory signaling.
facts.quote: There may have been inflatable air sacs flanking it for both visual and auditory signaling.

facts.statement: Kritosaurus shared its environment with non-dinosaur species including the giant pterosaur Quetzalcoatlus, fishes, amphibians, lizards, turtles like Adocus, and mammals like Alphadon and Mesodma.
facts.quote: Non-dinosaur species that had shared the same environment with Kritosaurus included the giant pterosaur Quetzalcoatlus, various species of fishes and rays, amphibians, lizards, turtles like Adocus, and multiple species of mammals like Alphadon and Mesodma.

facts.statement: The genus Kritosaurus was named by Brown in 1910.
facts.quote: genus_authority: Brown, 1910

facts.statement: The species Kritosaurus navajovius was named by Brown in 1910.
facts.quote: species_authority: Brown, 1910

facts.statement: The name Kritosaurus is sometimes misinterpreted as "noble lizard," referencing the presumed Roman noble profile of the fragmented and originally restored flat nasal region.
facts.quote: Su nombre es malinterpretado a veces como "lagarto noble", en referencia la presunta "nariz aguileña" que se relaciona con los nobles romanos del perfil de la región nasal que se encontró en fragmentos, y desarticulada siendo restaurada originalmente como plana.

facts.statement: The taxonomy of Kritosaurus is complicated and historically includes Gryposaurus, Anasazisaurus, and Naashoibitosaurus.
facts.quote: Su taxonomía se ve envuelta en una complicada historia donde también se incluyen a Gryposaurus, Anasazisaurus, y Naashoibitosaurus.

facts.statement: Kritosaurus lived at the end of the Cretaceous Period, approximately 73 million years ago during the Campanian, in what is now North America.
facts.quote: que vivió a finales del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente 73 millones de años, en el Campaniense, en lo que hoy es Norteamérica.

facts.statement: Kritosaurus had a special adaptation in its snout that resulted in a wide tip.
facts.quote: Kritosaurus presentaba una adaptación especial en el hocico, que resultaba ancho en su extremo.

facts.statement: Kritosaurus walked on both two and four legs.
facts.quote: Caminaba sobre tanto en dos como en cuatro patas

facts.statement: Its head was narrow with a bump on the crown containing air passages that allowed it to emit sounds.
facts.quote: su cabeza era estrecha con un bulto en la corona, con conductos por los que pasaba aire y le permitía emitir sonidos con él

facts.statement: The type species K. navajovius measured 10 meters in length and weighed around 4 tons.
facts.quote: la especie tipo, K. navajovius, tenía una longitud de 10 metros y un peso de alrededor de 4 toneladas

facts.statement: A specimen found in Sabinas, Coahuila, Mexico, originally known as "Sabinosaurio," measures 11 to 12 meters in length, making it larger than the type species.
facts.quote: un espécimen encontrado en Sabinas Coahuila, México, originalmente conocido como "Sabinosaurio", le arrebata el título con sus 11 a 12 metros de longitud

facts.statement: The skull length is estimated at 87 centimeters from the top of the beak to where the quadrate articulates with the lower jaw at the back of the skull.
facts.quote: La longitud del cráneo se estima en 87 centímetros desde el pico superior en donde el cuadrado articula con la mandíbula inferior en la parte posterior del cráneo

facts.statement: Potential diagnostic features of Kritosaurus include a predentary without toothed crenulation, a sustained downward curve at the lower beak insertion, and a heavy, somewhat rectangular maxilla.
facts.quote: Potenciales características de diagnóstico de Kritosaurus incluye un predentario sin la crenulación dentada, una curva hacia abajo sostenida en la inserción del pico inferior, y un pesado, algo rectangular maxilar

facts.statement: According to Prieto-Márquez's 2013 re-diagnosis, Kritosaurus is distinguished by an extensive dorsolateral maxillary margin, a jugal with an orbital constriction deeper than the infratemporal, a larger infratemporal fenestra with a dorsal margin elevated above the orbital dorsal margin in adults, frontal bone participation in the orbital margin, and paired caudal parasagittal processes of the nasals resting on the frontal bones.
facts.quote: Según Prieto-Márquez, quien volvió a diagnosticar este género en 2013, Kritosaurus se puede distinguir en función de las siguientes características: la longitud del margen dorsolateral del maxilar es extensa, el yugal presenta una constricción orbitaria que es más profunda que la infratemporal, la fenestra infratemporal es mayor que la órbita y tiene un margen dorsal que está muy elevado por encima del margen orbitario dorsal en adultos, el hueso frontal participa en el margen orbital, la presencia de procesos parasagitales caudales pareados de las nasales que descansan sobre los huesos frontales

facts.statement: In 1904, Barnum Brown discovered the type specimen, AMNH 5799, of Kritosaurus near Ojo Alamo, San Juan County, New Mexico, USA.
facts.quote: En 1904, Barnum Brown descubrió el espécimen tipo, AMNH 5799 de Kritosaurus cerca de Ojo Álamo, Condado de San Juan, Nuevo México, Estados Unidos

facts.statement: Initially unable to correlate the stratigraphy accurately, by 1916 Brown could establish it as belonging to the De-na-zin Member of the Kirtland Formation in the Campanian.
facts.quote: Inicialmente no pudo correlacionar la estratigrafía con exactitud, pero en 1916 podía establecerlo como de qué ahora se conoce como en el Miembro De-na-zin de la Formación Kirtland en el Campaniano

facts.statement: Brown initially named it Nectosaurus, but that name was already used; Jan Versluys inadvertently suggested the previous option, leading Brown to retain the species name using the combination K. navajovius.
facts.quote: Inicialmente lo llamó Nectosaurus, pero ese nombre ya había sido usado. Jan Versluys, quien visitó a Brown antes del cambio, inadvertidamente dejó escapar la opción anterior. Conservó el nombre de la especie aunque usando la combinación K. navajovius

facts.statement: The 1914 publication of the genus Gryposaurus with an arched nose changed Brown's view on the dinosaur's snout anatomy.
facts.quote: La publicación de 1914 del género con nariz de arco canadiense Gryposaurus hizo cambiar la visión de Brown sobre la anatomía de la nariz del dinosaurio

facts.statement: From that time until the 1990s, Kritosaurus included the type species K. navajovius, K. incurvimanus, and K. notabilis, the original type species of Gryposaurus.
facts.quote: Desde ese tiempo hasta los años 1990, Kritosaurus estuvo formado por la especie tipo K. navajovius, K. incurvimanus y K. notabilis, la especie tipo original de Gryposaurus

facts.statement: In 1984, Argentine paleontologist José Fernando Bonaparte et al. named K. australis based on hadrosaurid bones from the late Campanian to early Maastrichtian of the Los Alamitos Formation in Río Negro Province, Patagonia, Argentina.
facts.quote: En 1984, el paleontólogo argentino José Fernando Bonaparte et al. llamaron K. australis a huesos de un hadrosáurido de finales del Campaniano a principios del Maastrichiano, proveniente de la Formación Los Alamitos de la Provincia del Río Negro, Patagonia, Argentina

facts.statement: This species has been problematic, and its basal characteristics exclude it from belonging in Kritosaurus, as suggested by revisions in both editions of The Dinosauria.
facts.quote: Esta especie ha sido problemática y sus características basales lo excluyen de pertenecer en Kritosaurus, según lo sugerido por las revisiones en ambas ediciones de The Dinosauria

facts.statement: In 1992, Horner described two additional skulls from New Mexico that he considered belonging to Kritosaurus and demonstrated they were distinct from Gryposaurus.
facts.quote: Horner en 1992 describió dos cráneos más de Nuevo México que consideró pertenecientes a Kritosaurus y demostró que eran distintos a Gryposaurus

facts.statement: Adrian Hunt and Spencer G. Lucas placed each skull in its own genus, creating Anasazisaurus and Naashoibitosaurus.
facts.quote: Adrian Hunt y Spencer G. Lucas pusieron cada calavera en su propio género, creando Anasazisaurus y Naashoibitosaurus

facts.statement: In 1993, American paleontologists Adrian Hunt and Spencer G. Lucas named Anasazisaurus horneri.
facts.quote: Adrian Hunt y Spencer G. Lucas, paleontólogos estadounidenses , nombraron Anasazisaurus horneri en 1993

facts.statement: The name was derived from the Anasazi, an ancient Native American people, and the Greek word sauros, meaning "lizard."
facts.quote: El nombre se derivaba de los Anasazi, un antiguo pueblo nativo americano y la palabra griega sauros, "lagarto"

facts.statement: The holotype skull and only known specimen were collected in the late 1970s by a Brigham Young University field group working in San Juan County and is cataloged as BYU 12950.
facts.quote: El cráneo holotipo y el único espécimen conocido fue recolectado a fines de la década de 1970 por un grupo de campo de la Universidad Brigham Young que trabajaba en el condado de San Juan y se encuentra en catalogado BYU 12950

facts.statement: Not all authors agree with this; Thomas E. Williamson, in particular, defends Horner's original interpretation.
facts.quote: No todos los autores han convenido con esto, Thomas E. Williamson en particular defiende la interpretación original de Horner

facts.statement: Therefore, Prieto-Márquez considered Anasazisaurus a synonym of Kritosaurus but retained it as the distinct species K. horneri.
facts.quote: Por lo tanto, Prieto-Márquez consideró a Anasazisaurus como sinónimo de Kritosaurus, pero lo retuvo como la especie distinta K. horneri

facts.statement: Subsequent studies have confirmed that this species is a more modern synonym of Secernosaurus koerneri.
facts.quote: Estudios posteriores han confirmado que esta especie es un sinónimo más moderno de Secernosaurus koerneri

facts.statement: Horner originally assigned the Anasazisaurus skull to Kritosaurus navajovius, but Hunt and Lucas could not find any diagnostic features in the limited Kritosaurus material and judged the genus to be dubious.
facts.quote: Horner originalmente asignó el cráneo de Anasazisaurus a Kritosaurus navajovius, pero Hunt y Lucas no pudieron encontrar ninguna característica de diagnóstico en el material limitado de Kritosaurus y juzgaron que el género era un dudoso

facts.statement: Kritosaurus was a saurolophine hadrosaurid duck-billed dinosaur characterized by a flat head or solid crest.
facts.quote: Kritosaurus era una hadrosáurido saurolofininido, una pico de pato de cabeza plana o cresta sólida.

facts.statement: The closest relative of Kritosaurus navajovius is Anasazisaurus horneri, which is also known as Kritosaurus horneri.
facts.quote: El pariente más cercano de Kritosaurus navajovius es Anasazisaurus horneri también llamado Kritosaurus horneri

facts.statement: Kritosaurus forms the clade Kritosaurini with close relatives like Gryposaurus and Secernosaurus, which is part of the larger Saurolophinae clade.
facts.quote: que junto con parientes cercanos como Gryposaurus y Secernosaurus, forman un clado llamado Kritosaurini dentro del clado más grande Saurolophinae.

facts.statement: Barnum Brown described an undescribed species of Kritosaurus, likely Kritosaurus navajovius, from the Ojo Alamo, Javelina, and El Picacho formations since the 1930s.
facts.quote: Desde la década de 1930, Barnum Brown describió que una especie no descrita de Kritosaurus, el candidato más probable que era Kritosaurus navajovius, había habitado la Formación Maastrichtiense Ojo Álamo, la Formación Javelina en Texas y la Formación El Picacho

facts.statement: Kritosaurus was discovered in the De-na-zin Member of the Kirtland Formation, which dates to the Campanian stage of the Late Cretaceous, approximately 74 to 70 million years ago.
facts.quote: Kritosaurus fue descubierto en el Miembro De-na-zin de la Formación Kirtland. Esta formación data del Campaniense en el Cretácico Superior, hace aproximadamente 74 a 70 millones de años atrás

facts.statement: The genus Kritosaurus lived from the Santonian to the Maastrichtian stages, between 85.7 and 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Santonian to Maastrichtian (85.7 to 66 million years ago)

facts.statement: Kritosaurus was a large herbivore that alternated between bipedal and quadrupedal positions, using a sophisticated skull for chewing-like plant processing.
facts.quote: Como todo hadrosáurido, Kritosaurus fue un gran herbívoro que alternaba la posición bípeda con la cuadrúpeda, comiendo plantas con un sofisticado cráneo que permitía un movimiento similar a la masticación.

facts.statement: Kritosaurus had constantly replacing teeth packed in dental batteries, with only a handful of teeth in use at any given time.
facts.quote: Sus dientes se remplazaban constantemente y se encontraban empaquetados en baterías dentales, con solo un puñado de los mismos en uso al mismo momento.

facts.statement: Kritosaurus used a toothless horny beak at the front of its mouth to take vegetation, which was held in place by a skin structure functioning like cheeks.
facts.quote: El material vegetal era tomado por un pico córneo en la parte frontal de la boca que era desdentada, y mantenido en la boca por una estructura de piel de función similar a las mejillas.

facts.statement: Kritosaurus fed on plants reaching up to four meters in height.
facts.quote: Se alimentaba de las plantas que alcanzaban hasta cuatro metros de altura.

facts.statement: The nasal crest of Kritosaurus, whose true form is unknown, may have been used for social functions such as sex or species identification and social grading.
facts.quote: La cresta nasal de Kritosaurus, aunque que su forma verdadera es desconocida, se pudo haber utilizado para una variedad de funciones sociales, tales como identificación de sexos o especie y graduación social.

facts.statement: The nasal crest may have consisted of inflatable air sacs flanking it for visual and auditory signaling.
facts.quote: Puede haber estado compuestas de sacos de aire inflables que la flanquean para la señalización visual y auditiva.

facts.statement: The Kirtland Formation, where Kritosaurus fossils are found, is interpreted as a river plain that appeared after the retreat of the Niobrara Sea.
facts.quote: La Formación Kirtland es interpretada como una llanura fluvial, aparecida después que se retirara del Mar de Niobrara.

facts.statement: Conifers were the dominant plants in the habitat, and chasmosaurine ceratopsians appear to have been more common than hadrosaurids.
facts.quote: Las coníferas eran las plantas dominantes, y los chasmosaurínido parecen haber sido más comunes que los hadrosáuridos.

facts.statement: The geographic range of Kritosaurus remains in North America expanded with the discovery of bones from the Agujas Formation in Texas, Campanian age, which includes a skull.
facts.quote: El alcance geográfico de los restos de Kritosaurus en América del Norte se amplió con el descubrimiento de huesos de la Formación Aguja de Texas, del era de Campaniense, que incluye un cráneo.

facts.statement: A partial skull from Coahuila, Mexico, has been referred to Kritosaurus navajovius.
facts.quote: Además, un cráneo parcial de Coahuila , México , ha sido referido a K. navajovius.

facts.statement: It is unknown how Kritosaurus would have partitioned resources with the similar and contemporary Naashoibitosaurus if they were separate genera.
facts.quote: Si fueran géneros separados, cómo habría repartido recursos con el similar y contemporáneo Naashoibitosaurus es desconocido.

facts.statement: Fossils from the Ojo Alamo Formation could belong to an unknown hadrosaurid species or an undescribed specimen of Kritosaurus.
facts.quote: Estos fósiles podrían ser de una especie desconocida de hadrosáurido o un espécimen no descrito de Kritosaurus.
